readouts.source: A volcano erupts when pressure from dissolved gases drives magma toward the surface. Magma contains molten rock, crystals, and gases such as water vapor and carbon dioxide. As it rises, falling pressure allows bubbles to expand. Explosive eruptions eject ash and fragments of rock, while quieter eruptions produce lava flows. Scientists monitor ground movement, small earthquakes, and gas emissions to understand changes beneath a volcano. Ash can affect aviation and breathing, and volcanic soils can support farming.

readouts.source: A compiler translates a program from a source language into machine instructions. The lexer identifies tokens, and the parser organizes them into a syntax tree. The type checker verifies that operations use compatible values. An intermediate representation allows optimization passes to simplify expressions and remove unused computations. The backend selects instructions for a particular processor and assigns registers. A linker combines compiled objects with libraries and resolves external symbols. Debugging information connects the resulting instructions to locations in the original source code so a developer can inspect
